=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — buyer review

## Overall assessment

The Seller’s package leaves Wattlebridge exposed to paying **AUD 24 million for shares in a company that may still carry debt, transaction costs and unresolved operational liabilities**, while substantially restricting recourse. We should not treat the Seller’s “[STANDARD]”, “FINAL” or purported principal-level agreement labels as evidence that these terms are market, agreed or cleared. Those assertions require independent confirmation.

The immediate priorities are: **a debt-free completion and coherent price adjustment; effective Bluefen consent; a stronger Ironquay remedy; and a disclosure and liability regime that does not eliminate the protection being purchased.**

## Material issues and proposed pushback

### 1. Riverlark debt and the completion price

**Issue.** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding under Riverlark, and no final discharge is included. A release after Completion does not itself ensure that the debt is repaid at Completion. Buying the shares while the company remains indebted is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free baseline.

**Pushback.**

- Require repayment from Completion proceeds **at Completion**, directly to Riverlark under an agreed funds flow, with a current payout figure covering principal, interest, break costs and fees.
- Require binding payoff and release documentation delivered at Completion, including an undertaking and practical mechanism for prompt registration of security releases. Do not accept an unqualified promise to produce a release later.
- Ensure the AUD 24 million price and completion-accounts or other agreed adjustment mechanism deduct debt and debt-like items and deal consistently with cash, without double counting. Confirm whether AUD 24 million is the debt-free/cash-free enterprise value or the fixed equity price before finalising the mechanics.

### 2. Completion bonuses and other price leakage

**Issue.** DD-005 records AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses, omitted from the funds flow. Their treatment as Seller costs has not been implemented. Applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unknown. If Paperbark pays them after Completion without adjustment, Buyer bears a transaction-related cost.

**Pushback.** Require Seller to bear the bonuses and applicable on-costs, either by payment at Completion or a clear debt-like deduction/adjustment or targeted indemnity. Address conditionality, payment timing and amounts actually payable; avoid double recovery. Reconcile the signed employment terms and payroll calculations with the funds flow.

The three Sandbar renewals total **AUD 330,000**, but the record does not establish whether they are accrued, unavoidable, terminable or ordinary-course. Review DD-008 and DD-011 and underlying contracts before allocating them. Deduct or specifically protect against pre-Completion liabilities or transaction-triggered/non-ordinary costs as appropriate; do not automatically treat the whole amount as debt.

### 3. Bluefen change-of-control consent

**Issue.** Bluefen accounts for approximately AUD 3.6 million, or 30%, of FY26 revenue. No final written consent or evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions is included. Reasonable endeavours alone, and treating consent as satisfied merely on receipt of a letter, may leave Buyer with a conditional, ineffective or commercially damaging consent.

**Pushback.** Make Completion conditional on receipt of a valid, effective written consent satisfying clauses 11.2–11.3, with all conditions fulfilled or validly waived and no unacceptable changes, fees or loss of rights. Require Seller to obtain it by a long-stop date, with appropriate Buyer termination rights if not satisfied. Review any proposed consent and supporting evidence before acceptance.

### 4. Ironquay IP

**Issue.** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but does **not** independently establish non-payment. There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. An indemnity confined to the SOW3 payment may not cover loss of ownership or use rights, remediation or third-party claims.

**Pushback.** Before Completion, require evidence of cleared payment of all relevant fees and a valid confirmatory assignment or other satisfactory confirmation of title and rights. Expand the specific indemnity to cover losses arising from defective or challenged ownership, use rights and associated claims and remediation, not merely the fee. Negotiate an appropriate dedicated cap and survival period outside general warranty thresholds and knowledge/disclosure defences, subject to no double recovery.

### 5. Export/privacy incident

**Issue.** An export link went to an unintended external address and may involve approximately 1,240 records. Access, scope, notification obligations and loss remain unknown. It is neither established to be a confirmed breach nor safe to dismiss as immaterial.

**Pushback.** Require prompt investigation and preservation of evidence; establish access logs, recipient actions, affected data, containment and remediation. Obtain specialist assessment of applicable privacy, contractual and notification obligations and timing. Require disclosure of findings and material developments before Completion, and negotiate a tailored indemnity for pre-Completion incident-related losses and response costs, with suitable control of claims and cooperation provisions. Consider a Completion condition or other closing protection if the investigation reveals material exposure.

### 6. Warranty limitations and remedies

**Issue.** The Seller proposes a **20% general warranty cap (AUD 4.8 million)**, AUD 25,000 de minimis, and a **tipping-over basket that is actually excess-only**: once AUD 250,000 is exceeded, only the excess is recoverable. General claims expire after 18 months. Applying that package to all claims, including title and specific indemnities, could leave Buyer materially undercompensated. The Seller’s market assertions do not establish what is appropriate for this transaction.

**Pushback.**

- Seek a higher general cap and a longer notification period; negotiate the thresholds down and seek a **first-dollar/tipping basket**, not an excess-only deductible.
- Exclude fundamental warranties—particularly title, capacity and authority—from general thresholds, basket and short survival. Seek a cap up to the purchase price and a materially longer period, subject to applicable law.
- Give tax warranties and any tax covenant a dedicated regime aligned with relevant assessment periods; give IP warranties an appropriately longer period and tailored protection.
- Expressly carve specific indemnities, price adjustments and completion obligations out of the general warranty limitations unless a particular limitation is expressly negotiated for them.
- Preserve remedies for fraud and other liabilities that cannot lawfully be excluded, and avoid broad exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language inadvertently extinguishing agreed contractual protections or legally available remedies. Have Australian counsel confirm the drafting and applicable law.

### 7. General disclosure and Buyer knowledge

**Issue.** The Seller seeks to disclose the entire data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records, and to bar claims for matters Buyer or advisers knew **or could discover**. This shifts the risk of unidentified material to Buyer and may neutralise warranties, including through information buried in documents.

**Pushback.** Limit disclosure to matters **fairly disclosed** in the disclosure letter with sufficient detail and specificity to identify the nature and scope of the risk against the relevant warranty. Reject general data-room and public-register disclosure and constructive knowledge or “discoverable” standards. If any actual-knowledge qualification is agreed, restrict it to specified individuals’ actual knowledge and define its interaction with fair disclosure. It should not defeat specific indemnities, title protection or agreed completion obligations.

### 8. Share title and other contractual matters

**Title.** DD-012 is evidence that Harbourglass is recorded as holder of all issued shares; it is not conclusive verification of unencumbered title or the full capital position. Check the register and constitutional/corporate records, share issues, options and other rights, and security searches. Require appropriate title and capacity warranties, transfer and corporate approvals, and releases of encumbrances at Completion.

**Office lease and Mossvale.** DD-007 identifies a lease **notification**, not a demonstrated consent requirement. DD-009 restricts assignment but does not establish that a share sale requires Mossvale consent. Confirm the full provisions and satisfy any applicable notification obligations; do not assume either consent is required without further analysis.

## Recommended negotiation and diligence priorities

1. **Before signing or as firm Completion conditions:** settle the debt-free/cash-free price and funds flow; obtain Riverlark payoff/release arrangements and effective Bluefen consent; resolve Ironquay payment and IP title.
2. **Allocate identified exposures:** put the bonuses and on-costs on Seller’s account; investigate the export incident and negotiate targeted protection; verify the Sandbar renewals before determining their price treatment.
3. **Restore meaningful recourse:** renegotiate caps, thresholds and survival; separate fundamental, tax, IP and specific-indemnity protection from the general regime; narrow disclosure, knowledge, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.
4. **Complete verification:** confirm share capital and encumbrances, review the underlying contracts and consent conditions, and confirm lease notification requirements. Reconcile all agreed protections with the complete SPA, disclosure letter and completion funds flow.
